commits.author: Daeron
commits.message:
SECURE-PROTOCOLS-120 Add optional PKCE support for private_key_jwt (#13561)

* SECURE-PROTOCOLS-120 Add optional PKCE support for private_key_jwt

Require independent client assertion and PKCE verification for confidential
OIDC clients that submit a code challenge. Gate new combined authorizations
behind a default-off flag while enforcing previously issued challenges
regardless of the flag's current value.

Validate S256 inputs, reject unsolicited verifiers, and report PKCE failures
as invalid_grant. Preserve legacy authentication modes, add challenge-presence
analytics, and document partner integration and safe rollout and rollback.

Add focused form and end-to-end coverage, including disabling the flag
between authorization and token redemption. Keep production controllers and
shared test helpers unchanged.

changelog: Upcoming Features, OpenID Connect, Add optional PKCE protection for integrations using private_key_jwt authentication

* SECURE-PROTOCOLS-120 Clarify PKCE validation and review coverage

Name authentication and verification predicates by their responsibilities,
split verifier validation into focused methods, and keep partial or empty
PKCE parameters subject to validation. Make nullable and PKCE-only service
provider configurations explicit in authorization specs.

Remove the unused feature-spec assignment and redundant configuration
comment. Remove partner guidance and rollout documentation from the IdP
repository so they can be maintained in their designated locations.

* Clarify validation errors for incomplete PKCE parameters

---------

commits.author: Tai Groot
commits.message:
Replace hand-rolled sleep polling in analytics_spec with Capybara sync (#13573)

* Replace hand-rolled sleep polling in analytics_spec with Capybara sync

analytics_spec waited for frontend-logged events with a loop that slept
100ms between expectation attempts and tracked a wall-clock deadline.
Replace it with AnalyticsHelper#wait_for_logged_event, which uses
Capybara's synchronize (10ms retry interval, bounded by the given wait)
and falls through to the normal expectation so a genuine miss still
reports the full event diff. The events in question are sent with
navigator.sendBeacon while the page unloads, so they legitimately race
the test thread; this keeps the wait but drops the coarse sleep.

changelog: Internal, Testing, Replace sleep polling for frontend analytics events

* Make the hybrid Socure last-attempt rate limit regression test deterministic (#13574)

* Make the hybrid Socure last-attempt rate limit regression test deterministic

The LG-16672 regression example stalled the final Socure result with
sleep(1) hoping the desktop's 5s poller would fire while the last attempt
was still being processed. That only exercised the race about one run in
five and cost a second every run. Hold the final result behind a Queue
instead: send the last DOCUMENTS_UPLOADED webhook in the background, wait
until the Socure stub is hit (rate limit already incremented, no result
stored), poll the link sent status endpoint from the desktop session and
assert it answers 401 rather than 429, then release the result.

Verified by reverting LinkSentPollController#max_attempts_reached? to its
pre-fix form: the example now fails every time (got 429), where before it
passed most runs.

changelog: Internal, Testing, Deterministically cover hybrid doc auth last-attempt rate limit race

* Retry chromedriver detached-node errors inside Capybara synchronize (#13575)

* Retry chromedriver detached-node errors inside Capybara synchronize

Capybara retries StaleElementReferenceError inside synchronize, but recent
Chrome/chromedriver reports the same condition (DOM replaced between find
and inspect) as a bare UnknownError with the message "Node with given id
does not belong to the document". Capybara does not recognise that, so any
have_css / visible? racing a navigation fails immediately instead of
retrying. This is the known-flake class behind request_letter_step_spec:37
and hybrid_socure_mobile_spec:1008 on main.

Teach Capybara::Node::Base#catch_error? to treat that error as retryable so
the existing wait handles it, and drop the local rescue in
InteractionHelper#wait_for_content_to_disappear that papered over the same
message.

changelog: Internal, Testing, Retry chromedriver detached node errors in Capybara waits

* Start the Capybara::Webmock proxy once per run instead of per feature example (#13576)

* Start the Capybara::Webmock proxy once per run instead of per feature example

rails_helper wrapped every feature example in Capybara::Webmock.start/stop.
start spawns a rackup process; stop sends it HUP and then sleeps a full
second waiting for it to exit. That is a hidden sleep(1) executed ~1,365
times per CI pipeline: about 23 CPU-minutes, 15% of all spec time, and
roughly 70% of the wall time of rack_test feature specs.

The proxy only exists so headless Chrome cannot reach the network; rack_test
examples never touch it, and nothing reads proxied_requests, so there is no
per-example state to reset. Start it lazily the first time a browser-driven
example runs and stop it once after the suite.

Measured locally (CAPYBARA_WAIT_TIME_SECONDS=5): users/sign_in_spec +
features/visitors 3m25s -> 51s; browser specs unchanged and still isolated
from the network.

changelog: Internal, Testing, Start the Capybara webmock proxy once per spec run

* Refresh knapsack_rspec_report.json from a current pipeline (#13577)

The committed report dated from June and covered 1,122 of the 1,289
current spec files. The 190 missing files included several of the
slowest feature specs (in_person_spec, hybrid_mobile_ddp_spec,
proofing_agent_activation_spec, ...), which knapsack can only round-robin
without timing data. Result: spec shards ranged from 5.9 to 13.3 minutes
in pipeline 207321 while the mean was 7.1.

This report is taken from the coverage artifact of pipeline 207333, the
first run that includes the per-example Capybara::Webmock proxy fix, so
its per-file weights reflect the timing profile the suite now has (the
fix shifted time away from rack_test-heavy files). Replaying knapsack's
distribution against those measured times: slowest shard 6.4 -> 5.8
minutes and fastest 2.2 -> 4.6, i.e. shards are now within ~1 minute of
each other instead of ~4. No change to what runs.

spec/simplecov_merger.rb already produces this file on every pipeline;
it just never gets committed back.

changelog: Internal, Testing, Refresh knapsack timing report so spec shards balance

commits.author: Tai Groot
commits.message:
Replace sleep(5) in in_person_spec with a deterministic poll assertion (#13572)

Stacked on #13571 (base branch `fix-account-reset-email-flakes`); part of the spec race-condition / sleep-removal series.

## 🛠 Summary of changes

`spec/features/idv/in_person_spec.rb` had a `sleep(5)` (the client poll interval) followed by a negative assertion that the desktop had *not* advanced after re-sending the link. That is a wall-clock-gated negative assertion: slow, and it proves nothing if the poller happens to be late.

Replaced with a deterministic check of the same behaviour: hit the status endpoint the poller uses (from the browser session, via a new `DocAuthHelper#link_sent_poll_status` helper) and assert it answers `202` — the poller only advances on `200` — and assert server-side that the IPP enrollment was cancelled. Same coverage, ~5s faster, no timing dependence.

## 📜 Testing Plan

- [x] `spec/features/idv/in_person_spec.rb:522` 4/4 green locally (both `CAPYBARA_WAIT_TIME_SECONDS=0` and `=5`)
- [x] rubocop clean

commits.author: Tai Groot
commits.message:
Fix flaky account reset email feature specs (#13571)

The account reset feature specs called
GrantAccountResetRequestsAndSendEmailsJob#perform with Time.zone.today (a
Date) while production passes Time.zone.now. The job compares the value
against the requested_at timestamp in SQL, so the Date is coerced to
midnight UTC. Zonebie randomizes Time.zone per rspec process; whenever it
picks a zone with a negative UTC offset and the run happens after 00:00 UTC
but before local midnight, "today" in that zone is a day behind UTC, tvalue
lands before requested_at, the query matches nothing, no granted email is
sent, and open_last_email either raises "No email has been sent!" or opens
the request email (no cancel/delete token link). Passing Time.zone.now
matches the production job arguments and makes the comparison independent
of the randomized zone.

Reproduced deterministically with ZONEBIE_TZ=Montevideo (all four examples
fail before, pass after) and 20 unforced runs.

changelog: Internal, Testing, Fix account reset email spec flakiness

Render an NDS form-page variant of users/backup_code_setup#create when
nds_layout? is true; the default branch is byte-identical to before. The
codes render in a two-column card grid with copy, download and print
actions, followed by a required flat-checkbox acknowledgment card and a
gated Continue submit (PATCH to the continue path); the multi-MFA flow
keeps its choose-another-method delete as a tertiary action. Exposes the
account-creation helpers the NDS header progress needs and wires the
page into the dev NDS explorer.

changelog: Upcoming Features, Sign In, Add the NDS save-your-backup-codes page

commits.author: AppleLamps
commits.message:
docs: fix MODEL_CARD usage example to use real ChatGuard API

The example called `guard.redact(...)` and destructured `{ redacted }`,
neither of which exists. ChatGuard's public scrub method is `protect()`,
which returns a ScrubResult whose field is `text` (not `redacted`).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: tai
commits.message:
Fix NER offset recovery for duplicate digit substrings.

Use tokenizer token indices to map BIO labels to char offsets instead of
indexOf on folded text, which attached address BUILDING_NUMBER tokens to
phone digit runs when the same substring appeared twice. Add a regression
test and expose tokenize on the classifier adapter.

Co-authored-by: ed <ed@ndstudio.gov>
